Assalamu alaykum.
I am writing to you from Uzbekistan with a heart full of pain and hope. I do not know if my words will reach you, but I am holding on to even the smallest chance that they might.

As a father, it is heartbreaking to see my loved ones struggle like this. I try to stay strong for them, but inside I feel helpless. I carry this pain silently, because I have no other choice.
We are also facing health problems, and without proper living conditions, it is becoming harder for us to recover. We are not asking for luxury — only for a chance to live a normal, safe, and healthy life.

In our country, this amount is beyond our reach. It remains only a dream unless someone kind-hearted helps us.
I am asking you with deep respect and sincerity: if there is any way you can help us, or guide us toward help, please do not ignore our situation.
You may never meet us, but your kindness could become the reason our lives change forever.
May God bless you and your family with health, peace, and endless goodness.
With deep respect and hope,

caption:
The most surreal and humbling day of my career. 

My FIRST Golden Globe nomination! 🙏🏾🤎

THANK YOU @goldenglobes for this incredibly inspiring honor and acknowledgment of the story we told and souls we bared. 

What a privilege to be included with such an insane cadre of artists whose extraordinary performances all have raised the standard. 

Getting the opportunity to live in the skin of Mark Kerr was the most life changing and beautiful experience of my career - and my gratitude runs deep to Mark for trusting me with his story and ultimately, trusting me with his life. 

Celebrating my brother and our fearlessly empathetic director, the brilliant and hungry Benny Safdie @bowedtie - and I count my lucky stars to have the greatest scene partner of all time, Emily Blunt, whose RAW, heart wrenching, and lived in performance as Dawn Staples, moves us all to aching tears. 

Finally, I’m still in awe of the transformative, prosthetic make-up work of the great, Kazu Hiro @kazustudios and all of the Smashing Machine crew who truly became a family and left it all on the screen. 

This experience was life changing and unlocking. 

Thank you to ALL OF YOU for “ walking down this road with me” on this wild and unpredictable journey of life… 

and art. 

🤎🙏🏾

In All’s Fair, I play a lawyer who sees firsthand how the legal system can either empower women or leave them behind. But in the real world, the “price of justice” is a barrier that many women simply cannot afford. 

This Friday, March 27, I’m auctioning off my Season 1 wardrobe from All’s Fair to help close that gap. 100% of net sales will go directly to the Legal Aid Foundation of Los Angeles to fund their free legal services for women who are fighting for their safety, their children, and their futures. 

The right to a lawyer shouldn’t depend on the balance of your bank account. For many women, legal aid is the only bridge to a restraining order, a fair custody agreement, or the chance to rebuild a life from scratch. Supporting survivors means more than just helping them leave; it means ensuring our justice system recognizes the reality of abuse. 

We are making sure that “justice for all” actually means all. 

The auction will run from Friday, March 27 at 9am PT through Sunday, March 29 at midnight on @kardashiankloset.

caption:
Get the gin and juice ready, Snoop Dogg is officially getting the biopic treatment.⁠
⁠
Announced at CinemaCon, Snoop is set to begin production this summer, with a 2027 theatrical release on the way.⁠
⁠
Jonathan Daviss will step into the role of a young Snoop (born Calvin Broadus Jr.), while Craig Brewerm known for 'Hustle & Flow,' is directing. The film is also backed by Brian Grazer, the same producer behind '8 Mile.'⁠
⁠
Snoop made it clear this one’s personal, calling it his turn after 'Straight Outta Compton' helped tell the story of West Coast rap’s rise.⁠
⁠
The film is expected to be rated R and will follow his journey from Long Beach to hip-hop icon, a story that spans decades, from Doggystyle to his current era, still dropping music and popping up everywhere from TV to the Olympics.⁠
⁠
More details on the biopic are at the link in bio.

Dear Mr. Stallone,

My name is Quvonch Ismoilov, and I am from Uzbekistan. I grew up watching your movies, and your words have always lit my path. One line in particular has been engraved in my heart:
“It’s not about how hard you can hit. It’s about how hard you can get hit and keep moving forward.”
I have learned to look at life this way.

Now I am creating my own brand — Cressor. This brand is aimed at producing premium-class clothing. I am giving all my passion and energy to make high-quality clothes, because I don’t want to live the same kind of life as those around me.

All of my family members work in government jobs. Their lives are the same: from early morning until late evening at work, coming home exhausted, with little time left for their children. Even weekends are often taken up by work. They are preparing me for the same path, but I don’t want that life.

My dream is to become a billionaire. Not for the money itself, but for freedom: freedom of time, freedom to care for my family, and the freedom to help others. As you once said:
“Every champion was once an ordinary man. And why is he a champion? Because he never gave up.”
I feel the same — I will not give up.

Mr. Stallone, I believe in myself, but it is difficult to achieve this alone. I also need someone who believes in me, a sponsor. That is why I sincerely ask you: please be my sponsor. With your support, I can take Cressor to great heights. One day, my success will not only benefit me, but also others — perhaps even your grandchildren and great-grandchildren.

Also, I want to be honest with you: I am asking you for help for the future — please, help me. If I fail to get this brand off the ground, I may become like a lost person who has given up on dreams. Please help me.

Here is the website of my Cressor brand: it is not ready yet, but I am still working on it —
👉 https://cressor.netlify.app

Thank you for inspiring me with your films, your words, and your life. You have shown the world that determination brings victory. I want to walk the same path.

With respect,
Quvonch Ismoilov
Uzbekistan

Dear Jean-Claude Van Damme,
You played a villain once.
But not just any villain.
You played Jean Vilain — a man destined for evil, even by name.
Most people saw a bad guy.
But I saw something else:
A man choosing to lose, on his own terms.
While others saw fists and kicks,

But from you.
From the man who showed the world what it means to fight with body and soul.
In your final scene,
You didn’t resist death.
You embraced it.
Not as weakness…
But as dignity.
You weren’t defeated.
You walked into your end like a samurai —
With pride, pain, and purpose.
That moment wasn’t about the hero winning.
It was about the villain saying:
“You all forgot me…
But I never forgot who I am.”
Your silence screamed louder than any monologue.
Your presence forced the entire screen to breathe.
You gave your co-stars a lesson — without a single word.
That…
Was acting.
That…
Was legacy.
That…
Was Van Damme.
Respect,
From someone who truly saw you.
– A real fan.
